title: Faggots and Peas
subtitle: Pork mince and offal balls baked in a rich gravy, served with mushy peas
excerpt: Seasoned pork mince balls wrapped in caul and baked in beef gravy until dark and sticky. Served with mushy peas for a proper old-fashioned British supper.
sourceNotes: Traditional Midlands and Welsh faggot recipe using pork mince, sage and onion, adapted from British household cookery sources.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the cooked faggots in their gravy. Defrost overnight and reheat gently in the oven at 170C for 20 minutes.
recipe.batchNotes: Double easily. Faggots improve overnight in the fridge as the gravy thickens.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make and bake the day before. Reheat covered in the oven before serving.

content.text: Faggots are British pork mince balls seasoned with sage and onion, baked in a rich gravy. Chilling the shaped faggots for 30 minutes before baking helps them keep their shape. Do not skip this step or they may spread in the tin.

items.prepNote: tinned or made from dried split peas

content.text: Melt the butter in the frying pan over a medium heat. Cook the onion and bacon for 6 minutes until soft. Leave to cool for 10 minutes.
Combine the pork mince, cooled onion and bacon, breadcrumbs, sage, nutmeg and beaten egg in a large bowl. Season well. Mix until everything is evenly combined.
Divide the mixture into 8 equal portions. Roll each into a firm ball. Place in the roasting tin. Chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 190C. Whisk the flour into the cold beef stock. Add the Worcestershire sauce. Pour around the faggots in the tin.
Bake for 50 minutes, basting the faggots with the gravy twice during cooking. They should be dark brown on top.
Warm the mushy peas in a small saucepan. Season and serve alongside the faggots with plenty of the gravy poured over.

items.symptom: The faggots spread out flat in the tin.
items.cause: The mixture was too wet or they were not chilled before baking.
items.fix: Add a little more breadcrumb to firm the mixture. Always chill the shaped faggots for 30 minutes.

items.symptom: The gravy is too thin at the end.
items.cause: Too much stock was used or the oven temperature was too low.
items.fix: Pour the gravy into a small saucepan and reduce over a high heat for 3 to 4 minutes.

items.cause: They were baked uncovered for too long without basting.
items.fix: Baste every 15 minutes. Cover loosely with foil for the last 15 minutes if the tops are very dark.
